newsitem.title: BELGIUM: YEARENDER - Belgian shares seen up 10 to 20% in 1997.
newsitem.headline: YEARENDER - Belgian shares seen up 10 to 20% in 1997.

text.p: Leading Belgian shares are set to climb by 10 to 20 percent in 1997, with selected cyclicals and insurance stocks likely to be top performers as the economy picks up and interest rates stay relatively low, analysts said.
"The basic scenario is recovery in Europe and a slowdown in the United States," said Etienne Raemdock, analyst at Belgian brokerage Vermeulen Raemdonck.
"Our strategy is focused on good stories...with stock-picking in cyclicals," he added.
Most economists expect the Belgian economy to grow by about 2.2 percent in 1997. Vermeulen-Raemdonck forecasts company earnings growth of 10.6 percent compared to 9.8 percent in 1996.

Stefan Casteleyn, analyst at Corluy and Co said the prospect of economic recovery, stable interest rates and a background of mergers and takeovers in Europe could send the Bel-20 share index .BFX 20 percent higher.
Currently the index stands at around 1,890 points.

At the same time, he said, Belgian shares looked cheap when estimated 1997 dividend yields were compared to current 10-year bond yields which were now on a ratio of 1.6 versus an average of 2.2 over the past decade.
"The stock market has not really become aware that interest rates are so low," Casteleyn added.
Several analysts highlighted oil, petroleum and chemicals company Petrofina, cement maker CBR and chemicals firm Tessenderlo as cyclicals which would star next year.
Petrofina stock has already begun catching up after lagging behind partly due to pressure from over-the-counter derivatives.

Analysts cited expectations of a stronger dollar, higher oil prices as well as better refining margins as reasons for optimism. They also noted the company had started making itself more visible to shareholders.
Insurer Fortis as well as Kredietbank -- considered the cheapest in its sector -- and KB's related units were backed as insurers/financials likely to outperform the market.
Energy supplier Electrabel would be attractive for its yield.

"Fortis is a growth story rather than interest rate story," said analyst Luc Van der Elst at Generale Bank, adding Fortis had potential for more takeovers after the group recently bought investment bank MeesPierson.
Other cyclicals in favour were chemicals stock Solvay and steel cord and wire maker Bekaert.

Bekaert suffered in recent sessions after the company warned 1996 earnings would be around breakeven due to a large provision for restructuring, but several analysts take a positive long-term view of the stock.
Analyst Martine Glineur at Mignon, Hanart, Declerck saw the Bel-20 rising up to 10 percent by the end of the year, though predicted some consolidation at the start of 1997.
Among retailers, Delhaize was rated a 'buy' by several houses, but there was no sign of much improvement in consumption levels to benefit the sector as a whole.

Smaller stocks analysts backed as outperformers next year included car distributor D'Ieteren, plastic products maker Deceuninck, investment holding Belcofi and Telinfo, a financial holding company with interests in telecommunications.
